7404-john-james-audubon.title: John James Audubon
7404-john-james-audubon.creator: Unknown
7404-john-james-audubon.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Both men were famous pedestrians and often walked hundreds of miles at a stretch. They were natural explorers and voyagers. They loved Nature at first hand, and not merely as she appears in books and pictures. They both kept extensive journals of their wanderings and observations.

arxiv-2012-05490.title: PARRoT: Predictive Ad-hoc Routing Fueled by Reinforcement Learning and Trajectory Knowledge
arxiv-2012-05490.creator: Benjamin Sliwa, Cedrik Schüler, Manuel Patchou, and Christian Wietfeld
arxiv-2012-05490.description: Abstract Swarms of collaborating UAV that utilize ad-hoc networking technologies for coordinating their actions offer the potential to catalyze emerging research fields such as autonomous exploration of disaster areas, demand-driven network provisioning, and near field packet delivery in ITS .

arxiv-2112-05918.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Amir Mafi and Dler Naderi. arxiv-2302-05577.title: α \alpha -induction for bi-unitary connections
arxiv-2302-05577.creator: Yasuyuki Kawahigashi
arxiv-2302-05577.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yasuyuki Kawahigashi. The tensor functor called α \alpha -induction produces a new unitary fusion category from a Frobenius algebra object, or a Q Q -system, in a braided unitary fusion category. In the operator algebraic language, it gives extensions of endomorphism of N N to M M arising from a subfactor N ⊂ M N\subset M of finite index and finite depth which gives a braided fusion category of endomorphisms of N N . It is also understood in terms of Ocneanu’s graphical calculus.

arxiv-2307-00184.title: Personality Traits in Large Language Models
arxiv-2307-00184.creator: Gregory Serapio-García, Mustafa Safdari, Clément Crepy, Luning Sun, Stephen Fitz, Peter Romero, Marwa Abdulhai, Aleksandra Faust, Maja Matarić
arxiv-2307-00184.description: Abstract The advent of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized natural language processing, enabling the generation of coherent and contextually relevant human-like text. As LLMs increasingly power conversational agents used by the general public world-wide, the synthetic personality traits embedded in these models, by virtue of training on large amounts of human data, is becoming increasingly important.

arxiv-2407-10803.title: DINO Pre-training for Vision-based End-to-end Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2407-10803.creator: Shubham Juneja, Povilas Daniušis, Virginijus Marcinkevičius
arxiv-2407-10803.description: Abstract In this article, we focus on the pre-training of visual autonomous driving agents in the context of imitation learning. Current methods often rely on a classification-based pre-training, which we hypothesise to be holding back from extending capabilities of implicit image understanding.

arxiv-2410-11101.title: A Two-Stage Federated Learning Approach for Industrial Prognostics Using Large-Scale High-Dimensional Signals
arxiv-2410-11101.creator: Yuqi Su 1, Xiaolei Fang 2
arxiv-2410-11101.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yuqi Su 1, Xiaolei Fang 2. Industrial prognostics aims to develop data-driven methods that leverage high-dimensional degradation signals from assets to predict their failure times. The success of these models largely depends on the availability of substantial historical data for training. However, in practice, individual organizations often lack sufficient data to independently train reliable prognostic models, and privacy concerns prevent data sharing between organizations for collaborative model training.

arxiv-2503-05493.title: Benchmarking LLMs in Recommendation Tasks: A Comparative Evaluation with Conventional Recommenders CCS: Information systems Recommender systems CCS: Information systems Language models CCS: General and reference Evaluation
arxiv-2503-05493.creator: Qijiong Liu, Jieming Zhu, Lu Fan, Kun Wang, Hengchang Hu, Wei Guo, Yong Liu, Xiao-Ming Wu
arxiv-2503-05493.description: Abstract . In recent years, integrating large language models (LLMs) into recommender systems has created new opportunities for improving recommendation quality. However, a comprehensive benchmark is needed to thoroughly evaluate and compare the recommendation capabilities of LLMs with traditional recommender systems.

arxiv-2508-11510.title: Quantum Quench Dynamics in an Exactly Solvable Two-Dimensional Non-Fermi Liquid System
arxiv-2508-11510.creator: Hui Li, Run-Yu Chen, Wen-Yuan Liu, Yin Zhong, Hai-Qing Lin
arxiv-2508-11510.description: Abstract Understanding the behavior of non-Fermi liquids (NFLs) is an important topic in condensed matter physics. Here we introduce an exactly solvable multi-orbital model based on iron oxypnictides and the Hatsugai-Kohmoto model, and provide exact investigations of the 2D NFLs nonequilibrium physics present in this model.

arxiv-2511-23092.title: Does Self-Evaluation Enable Wireheading in Language Models?
arxiv-2511-23092.creator: David Demitri Africa Hans Ethan Ting
arxiv-2511-23092.description: Abstract Self-evaluation is increasingly central to language model training, underpinning techniques from Constitutional AI to self-refinement. We investigate whether coupling self-evaluation to reward signals creates incentives for wireheading, where agents manipulate the measurement process rather than optimizing the task. We first formalize conditions under which reward-channel control strictly dominates task-focused behavior in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs).

pmc-11509435.title: Inverse Shifting-PCR Modified by Capillary Electrophoresis for Detecting F8 int22h and int1h Inversions in Severe Hemophilia A Patients and Probable Carriers
pmc-11509435.creator: Rosa Michel Martínez-Contreras, Silvia Sofía García-López, Hilda Luna-Záizar, Ana Rebeca Jaloma-Cruz, Eleni Gavriilaki
pmc-11509435.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Globally, intron 22 inversions (Inv22s) of the factor VIII gene (F8) are the most frequent pathogenic variants and account for 45–50% of severe hemophilia A (SHA) cases, while intron 1 inversion (Inv1) explains 1–5% of SHA cases. The detection of both inversions by an inverse shifting-polymerase chain reaction (IS-PCR) is the first choice worldwide for the diagnosis of patients and carriers of SHA.

pmc-11597443.title: Mediterranean Diet in Older Adults: Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality from Observational and Interventional Studies—A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11597443.creator: Michela Furbatto, Diana Lelli, Raffaele Antonelli Incalzi, Claudio Pedone, Chengwen Sun
pmc-11597443.description: Background/Objectives: there is conflicting evidence on the role of the Mediterranean Diet (MD) in reducing the risk of long-term outcomes in older adults. The aim of our study was to assess the effectiveness of high adherence to MD in reducing all-cause mortality and cardiovascular outcomes among older adults. Methods: PubMed database was searched up to 31 May 2023.

pmc-11643502.title: Counteractive Effects of Copper Nanoparticles and Betacellulin on Ovarian Cells
pmc-11643502.creator: Alexander V. Sirotkin, Paula Romero-Navarro, Barbora Loncová, Zuzana Fabová, Michaela Bartušová, Abdel Halim Harrath, Francisco Alonso
pmc-11643502.description: Copper nanoparticles (CuNPs) are known to affect many ovarian cell functions. CuNPs, prepared using a chemical reduction method, were fully characterized by different means (TEM, DLS, XRD, Z potential, XPS, and AES). The resulting colloidal suspension contained needle-like CuNPs aggregates made of a core of metallic copper and an oxidized surface of Cu2O and CuO.

pmc-12614291.title: Few‐shot CBCT‐based synthetic CT generation with denoising diffusion probabilistic model
pmc-12614291.creator: Ping Lin Yeap, Xin Du, Meng Zhou, Andrew Hoole, Gillian C. Barnett, Rajesh Jena
pmc-12614291.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn adaptive cancer radiotherapy, treatment plans were periodically re‐optimised according to anatomical variations, with the goal of maintaining or improving clinical outcomes. This required high‐quality in‐room imaging for daily monitoring, tumour/organ segmentation and dose evaluation. However, in‐room cone‐beam computed tomography (CBCT) images suffered from inaccurate Hounsfield Unit (HU) values and poor image quality due to higher artifact presence and lower signal‐to‐noise ratio.

pmc-13102784.title: Integrating digital health and remote monitoring: emerging trends in cardiac rehabilitation research for chronic heart failure
pmc-13102784.creator: Chun-mei Gao, Ping Fu, Wei Du, Yong Li
pmc-13102784.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chronic heart failure (CHF) represents a major global public health burden. Traditional cardiac rehabilitation models face limitations due to geographical barriers, scheduling conflicts, and high dropout rates, leading to low participation and poor access. This perspective article argues that the deep integration of digital health and remote monitoring represents not merely a technical fix but a paradigm shift toward personalized, continuous, and preventive care. This approach employs a multi-layered framework that combines remote assessment, interactive intervention, and intelligent decision support.

pmc-13114545.title: Confinement-Tunable Spatial Distribution of Physisorbed Hydrogen in Defective Carbon Nanotube Bundles
pmc-13114545.creator: Shuming Yang, Kun Qiu, Gang Sun, Huaze Shen
pmc-13114545.description: Spatial confinement strongly affects matter by altering structural stability, relaxation times, and equilibrium properties. Interest in hydrogen storage within carbon nanotube bundles has grown because it addresses practical energy needs while revealing rich confined-fluid physics. Understanding how geometry and defects influence hydrogen structure and dynamics is essential to the development of effective storage materials.

pmc-13240071.title: Variation of Procalcitonin Level in Elective Cardiac Surgery at a Tertiary Cardiac Centre: A Prospective Longitudinal Study
pmc-13240071.creator: Prati Badan Dangol, Battu Kumar Shrestha, Suraksha Dhungana, Gaurab Mainali, Madanika Ghimire, Amrita Pandey
pmc-13240071.description: BackgroundProcalcitonin (PCT) levels often rise after cardiac surgery due to an ongoing postoperative inflammatory response. The changes in PCT levels are useful for the early detection of postoperative infections. We assessed the variation of procalcitonin levels in patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery at the leading tertiary cardiac centre to support clinical decision‐making and future studies in our setting.

pmc-13499440.title: Severe Uncontrolled Pancreatogenic Diabetes in a Patient With Prior Alcoholic Pancreatitis and Partial Pancreatectomy
pmc-13499440.creator: Reza Alavi, Youssef Elbanna, Thompson Trevor, Jesse Suarez
pmc-13499440.description: Pancreatogenic diabetes mellitus (type 3c diabetes mellitus, T3cDM) is an underrecognized form of secondary diabetes resulting from pancreatic exocrine disease, including chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic resection. It is frequently misclassified as type 2 diabetes mellitus, leading to delayed diagnosis and suboptimal management.
